title: Massive exchanged boomerang

target.description: Five-round AES with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted; the key schedule is unused and the construction applies to all three standard key lengths.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES master key and its key schedule.
setting.plaintext_model: Initial 2^11.5 diagonal structure; 2^29 CP used for the friend-pair stage and 2^31 adaptive ciphertext queries.
assumptions: Binomial independent-trial author model for both AES and ideal-permutation sides.
Experimental random-side control uses full 10-round AES, not independently sampled ideal permutations.
setting.reference_model: Equal-prior binary decision between the five-round fixed-secret-key AES permutation and an ideal random permutation using CP and adaptive inverse queries. Threshold K >= 1; the experiments instead use full ten-round AES as random-side control.

time.note: Source-native memory-access count, not normalized to AES encryptions.

data.note: Dominant ACC count; the additional chosen-plaintext costs are preserved in plaintext_model.

memory.note: The complete storage footprint is not quantified in Sections4–5.

preprocessing.note: Setup is included in total work unless separately stated.

success.description: Average of Pr[AES classified AES] and Pr[random classified random] at the source trial count and threshold K>=1.

review.scope: PDF pp.5–6 Table1, pp.11–15 Section4/Algorithm1/Table2. Checked the two-sided binomial model and experimental event separately.

components.description: One-sided value stated in Table1 footnote; different metric from primary two-sided average.
1000 tests per side: 780/1000 correct AES-side and 652/1000 correct control-side decisions; no local reproduction.

evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.

limitations: The probability is tied to the stated source model and trial count.
